messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired — HIGH — prod-public-api: HTTPS errors & ALB target flapping (PD-98321). Page sent to @oncall and escalation policy.
PagerDuty: Incident PD-98321 assigned to Alex (oncall).
Alex: acked in PD. I'm oncall — pulling quick metrics.
Sam: saw a spike starting ~18:30 UTC — 502s + TLS handshake_failure in multiple regions. Top customer reports intermittent TLS errors.
Jamie: doing quick probes. From my laptop (eu-west probe):
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/health
* Connected to api.redwood.example.com (34.202.11.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake error: alert handshake_failure
* Closing connection 0
```
Alex: interesting — us-east probe is returning 200. so this looks regional/partial.
Priya: running DNS checks, grabbing dig outputs.
Jamie: `dig +short api.redwood.example.com @8.8.8.8` returns two IPs for me: 34.202.11.45 and 3.126.77.9 (both are ALB frontends)
Jamie: from us-east probe the alias resolves to 3.126.77.9 only (the healthy new ALB). eu-west still sees 34.202.11.45 (old ALB).
Sam: old ALB (34.202.11.45) target-group health is flapping — several targets marked unhealthy with 502 from upstream. cert on old ALB looks expired/unmounted for the service cert.
Alex: quick summary: we rolled a DNS alias change earlier (blue->green) and TTL was low but some resolvers are still hitting the old ALB which currently has no valid cert and failing backend health checks. That causes TLS handshake failures for those clients and 502s at the ALB level.
Priya: impact estimate: ~3-7% error rate depending on resolver; primarily EU region customers and some corporate DNS caches. No data loss, but request failures to public API.
Alex: mitigation options: 1) attach valid cert to old ALB (fast), 2) roll back Route53 alias to previous record (can reduce footprint but DNS propagation will still take time), 3) adjust target group weights / re-register targets on old ALB (workaround).
Priya: I'm going to try attaching the existing cert to old ALB as a short-term fix. Alex, can you prepare to roll back Route53 if needed?
Alex: starting attach cert to old ALB now.
OpsBot: running IAM action to attach ACM cert arn:arn:aws:acm:us-east-1:123456:certificate/abcd1234 to elb/old-alb-34.202.11.45
OpsBot: attach completed (no errors).
Jamie: re-running curl from eu-west probe:
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/health
* Connected to api.redwood.example.com (34.202.11.45) port 443 (#0)
* SSL connection using TLSv1.2 / ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384
* Server certificate verified
* HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```
Sam: ALB target-group health: re-registering targets and forcing health-checks. status moving to healthy.
Alex: rolling back Route53 alias is on standby. not doing it now since cert attach fixed handshake. will keep TTL monitors.
Priya: monitoring metrics — error rate dropped to ~0.6% in eu-west within 3m of cert attach. request latency normal.
PagerDuty: PD-98321 acknowledged by Alex at 18:48 UTC.
incident-bot: Severity escalated to P1 because customer impact observed across regions. PD escalation policy triggered to secondary oncall.
Alex: notifying customer-success + engineering leads, will keep them updated. @Priya please capture all commands and times for postmortem.
Priya: got it — logging all steps. creating a follow-up ticket: INC-2026-2833 (postmortem + remediation).
Jamie: suggested long-term actions: enforce cert presence check as precondition for DNS cutover, add Route53 health-based failover for alias, increase automation around ALB target provisioning during deploys.
Sam: also recommend increasing canary window for DNS changes and lower TTLs pre-change (but remember caches).
Alex: handing off to night SRE to watch for 2 hours. Oncall for next shift: Jamie — do you want the handoff?
Jamie: taking handoff. monitoring dashboards + soak test for 30m, then degrade to 15-min checks.
Priya: owners assigned in INC-2026-2833: cert-check automation -> Sam; DNS deploy playbook -> Alex; postmortem -> Priya.
Alex: thanks everyone. leaving notes in incident timeline.
Jamie: will escalate immediately if error rate rises above 1.5% again.
incident-bot: PD-98321 marked as resolved in PagerDuty by Alex at 19:05 UTC (investigation complete, monitoring).
OpsBot: follow-up reminders created: postmortem due in 48h, PR for cert-check tests required before next DNS roll. :white_check_mark:
